title: Koine desktop contract
intro: Koine is a resident application with a shared resilient Swift provider framework and live bearer grants. Served-contract views describe the existing timestamp API. The future desktop contract now selects non-time capture with public Accessibility; its complete protocol and implementation remain open. Historical native investigations are labelled separately. The spec records acceptance and limitations.

discussion.title: Fresh callback sampling and actual right transfer
discussion.status: Conditional design — native premises and protocol remain open
discussion.summary: Separate candidate identity acquisition, the actual fresh foreground sample, continuous right ownership, peer authentication and live grant/resource adoption. Public XPC supplies a transfer primitive, not an established pre-acquisition budget. Native sampling and admission discriminators precede the resident protocol. No new native run, transport, packaging, reference or restart policy is adopted; the public AX scope agreement is unchanged.

updatedDiagrams.summary: Shows the conditional acquisition–sample–validation bracket, actual transfer ownership, adoption acknowledgment and unknown outcome after a possible send.

diagrams.title: Resource admission and the exchange conflict
diagrams.caption: Historical private-receive conflict, followed by the k104 scope decision. The local OOL counterexample and pinned explanatory XNU assessment of peek, queue count and overwrite establish no usable acquisition envelope; other mechanisms are not proved absent. No owned AX exchange ran. The human now accepts framework-managed AX reception without Koine hard acquisition limits, including resource pressure/failure, while retaining own state/work and capture-transfer bounds. Private exchange work is rejected for the first deliverable. See docs/verification/native-observation-receive.md#pre-copyout-admission-assessment.

diagrams.title: Receive acquisition before payload rejection
diagrams.caption: Measured local IPC in a disposable macOS 26.5 (25F71) VM. A self-sent 44-byte message acquired a distinct 128 KiB virtual-copy OOL mapping before the 64 KiB payload policy rejected it. The 32-byte inline control stayed queued; skipped destruction retained the mapping and exited 1 before final cleanup. Self audit agreement, whole-span mapping observations and local send-reference balance are bounded evidence, not AX authentication, physical-memory growth, arbitrary descriptor cleanup or universal impossibility. The private acquisition conflict remains unsolved; the human selected public AX and rejected the owned exchange for this deliverable in k104. See docs/verification/native-observation-receive.md#acquisition-budget-experiment.

diagrams.title: Historical private observation wire inspection
diagrams.caption: Historical investigation, rejected as a first-deliverable path in k104. Static loaded-byte evidence on macOS 26.5 (25F71). Request layouts, connection policy and native receive helpers are traced. CoreFoundation adopts the message voucher; HIServices injects the observer pointer into the context slot. Native success unmaps OOL info while rejected complex requests use message destruction. The proposed owned decoder borrows from one envelope owner. Actual audit evidence, execution context, bounded OOL acquisition and cleanup remain unvalidated; no owned exchange, closure, lifetime or publication barrier is established. See docs/verification/native-observation-receive.md.

diagrams.title: Historical private observation proposal
diagrams.caption: Historical conditional private-AX proposal, rejected for the first deliverable in k104. Its authenticated closure, lifetime-attributed reads, publication barrier, loss detection and native ingress/send premises were not established and are not current release gates. Local ownership, permanent reference withdrawal/non-reuse and bounded state/work remain in the public AX design, which explicitly accepts stale/misattributed reports and mistaken withdrawal. See docs/specs/machine.md#observation-and-retirement-protocol-proposal.

diagrams.title: Native targeting guarantee boundaries
diagrams.caption: Agreed future contract, not yet implemented: non-time callback capture and expiry with public macOS Accessibility. Wrong-target data/effects, stale or misattributed reports, mistaken withdrawal and framework AX acquisition without Koine hard memory/right limits are accepted, including resource pressure or Koine failure. Grants, Koine consent, known-dead refusal, permanent local withdrawal/non-reuse and own state/work bounds remain. Capture-transfer has separate acquisition and peer-authentication obligations. The complete protocol, lifecycle, references/restarts, public outcomes and acceptance remain open. See docs/specs/machine.md#native-targeting-discussion.

diagrams.title: Public AX scope and remaining adoption work
diagrams.caption: k104 explicitly selected public AX and rejected continued private endpoint/wire ownership for the first deliverable. Earlier diagnostics and static inspections remain bounded evidence; no owned observation exchange was completed. Capture/transfer, lifecycle consequence, public AX consent/local ownership and the complete client contract still need design, followed by implementation and signed/notarized acceptance. Reopening private AX needs an explicit product requirement and a concrete enforcement lead. See docs/verification/ax-endpoint-adoption.md.

diagrams.title: Top-level AX descriptors and downstream effects
diagrams.caption: Observed and inspected in TestAnyware clone koine-k68-routing on macOS 26.5 (25F71). TextEdit PID 772 owns both document and Open top-level descriptors; Open/Save content includes actual PID 781 with presenter 772. The Open panel fails the current provider's first-child AXWindow test. Direct document effects visibly minimize and restore; Open accepts the requests without observed minimization. AppKit's own registered callbacks resolve local data and dispatch to object methods; application activation reaches WindowServer or Launch Services. This establishes a conditional receiver contract, not arbitrary callback behavior, downstream death binding, admitted automatic restoration, or product adoption. Report, exact handler bounds, controls, frozen inputs and recommendation: docs/verification/ax-top-level-routing.md. The restoration view is unchanged context.

diagrams.title: Automatic restoration and AX client lifetime
diagrams.caption: Matched controls in TestAnyware clone koine-k69-restoration on macOS 26.5 (25F71). The identical minimizable target automatically terminates without AX contact before and after the AX arms; PID 1096 restores as 1119 with the same PSN. A single public AXRole reader exits 0 yet its target stays hidden and TAL-ineligible. Direct-only admission and positive minimize/readback/restore also leave the target live. Destroying only its owned client receive right does not recover eligibility; target task and endpoint remain live. The owned-client holders were stopped with status 143; no successor-effect or valid replacement-client branch ran. This is a bounded lifecycle conflict, not permanent inhibition, a universal impossibility result, or a completed action guarantee. Source, hashes, exact exits, controls and trade-offs: docs/verification/ax-automatic-restoration.md.

diagrams.title: AX receiver ownership and process transitions
diagrams.caption: Inspected and executed in TestAnyware clone koine-k65-receiver on macOS 26.5 (25F71). Default MSH allocation creates a local receive right and bootstrap gets a send right. Source release drops both local references. A signed/hardened holder admits PID 867 before exec; both old rights become dead names and every old-endpoint primitive refuses, with an unchanged successor witness. The later restoration view isolates AX-contact inhibition; the top-level routing view traces ordinary AppKit descriptors/callbacks and TextEdit panels. Downstream effect lifetime, custom handlers, arbitrary receive transfer and actual admitted restoration remain outside the bounded guarantee. No product adoption or schema change. See docs/verification/direct-ax-endpoint.md#receiver-allocation-and-transitions.

diagrams.title: Audited AX read and death ordering
diagrams.caption: Observed in disposable TestAnyware clone koine-k63-admission on macOS 26.5 (25F71). The actual AXRole request admits matching live tasks and refuses wrong-task controls. Live effects/focus succeed at PID 804; death before effects (813), between effects (816), and actual reuse (820 after 99,408 allocations) refuse every later direct primitive. A separate observer sees the successor unchanged. Each run has exit 0 and matching frozen-input hashes. Read-only means no write/action is requested; arbitrary getter internals are not constrained. This is a signed/hardened diagnostic inheriting VM-agent consent, not Koine consent or a shipping ABI. Receiver ownership/routing, exec/restoration, policy and client capture remain open. Full protocol, raw outputs and limits: docs/verification/direct-ax-endpoint.md.

diagrams.title: Direct AX effects through one retained endpoint
diagrams.caption: Executed in TestAnyware clone koine-k61-effects on macOS 26.5 (25F71): internal MIG read/set/action stubs used retained endpoint 12035 for PID 788. A separate public-AX/NSWorkspace observer saw minimize, restore and final focus. All live requests succeeded and the subsequent post-death write failed. No PID-based target-port refresh occurs during dispatch. This one-window Cocoa experiment does not establish receiver ownership, death between effects, exec/restoration, remote-element safety, audited admission or Koine consent attribution. The diagnostic is signed and hardened, inherits usable VM consent, and is not notarized. Exact source, ABI sites, input hashes, completed exit-0 record and limits are in docs/verification/direct-ax-endpoint.md.

diagrams.title: Direct AX endpoint: retention and responder matching
diagrams.caption: Observed in TestAnyware clone koine-k59-endpoint on macOS 26.5. The held port became a dead name and stayed dead after actual PID recycling. A separate header-only unknown-ID exchange received MIG_BAD_ID with a kernel audit trailer; a live retained-task read after the reply matched, and a wrong-task control rejected. Both diagnostics were Developer ID-signed and hardened, inherited usable AX consent, and were not notarized. No direct AX effect, exec, automatic restoration, client-event capture or client-to-Koine transfer was exercised. Sources, controls, hashes and limits are in docs/verification/direct-ax-endpoint.md.

diagrams.title: Why AX reconstruction does not bind native effects
diagrams.caption: Observed in TestAnyware clone koine-k56-binding on macOS 26.5: both privately reconstructed AX objects affected the successor at recycled PID 787. The holder created them before the original died and acquired no fresh AX objects afterward; separate processes witnessed both effects. The diagnostic was Developer ID-signed and hardened, but not notarized, and inherited usable AX access from the VM agent. This is platform evidence, not a Koine mistarget or product policy acceptance. The earlier public-held-object counterexample and full inputs, hashes, outputs, limitations and direct-endpoint lead are in docs/verification/retained-ax-binding.md.

diagrams.title: Why a public serial cannot identify the process
diagrams.caption: Observed in a macOS 26.5 TestAnyware clone with a diagnostic app. The same serial and boot identity resolved to PID 893, continued to report that PID after the process ended, then resolved to live PID 910 after automatic restoration. Captured sources, hashes and native output are in docs/verification/process-serial-lifetime.md. The human requires expiry with the original process, so PSN plus boot identity is ruled out. This does not establish unrelated-application serial reuse, actual PID reuse, or native Accessibility action safety.

diagrams.title: Fresh callback sample and continuous transfer ownership
diagrams.caption: Conditional source-grounded design, not a native result or adopted mechanism. The actual foreground observation must occur after acquiring the continuously held identity and before successful validation; invoking a getter does not establish freshness. Compare pre-held candidates with acquire-then-resample. Sender success releases only after matching owned-adoption acknowledgment; possible-send uncertainty and cleanup need the selected protocol. Sampling, hard transfer admission and authenticated resident packaging remain native design work. Peer attribution does not remotely attest callback provenance. See docs/verification/callback-capture-transfer.md. The public AX guarantee boundary is unchanged.

diagrams.title: Resident application and client boundary
diagrams.caption: Agreed runtime responsibility view: one resident Koine application contains the native UI, server and providers. Closing its management window leaves the listener and observation running. The native UI keeps management authority in process; HTTP clients present bearer credentials backed by live grants. Providers share that process and its OS permissions. The shared resilient Swift framework is agreed.

diagrams.title: Source packages and interface dependencies
diagrams.caption: Agreed application/framework composition, shown as package dependencies rather than deployment containers. Koine supplies one shared provider framework image, Machine invokes its contracts, and separately built providers conform to them. Published Swift types and protocols carry the compatibility promise; GraphQL-library types remain private. The client owns its GraphQL adapter; no Koine-owned client helper is required for this deliverable.

diagrams.title: Discover windows, derive choices, focus one
diagrams.caption: Served timestamp API: query before choices and resolve an opaque reference before acting. Its exact-target receipt meaning must change to the agreed public-AX focus attempt and framework observations; this diagram does not specify the replacement wire fields. See docs/specs/machine.md#native-targeting-discussion. Capability denial and missing Koine consent stay distinct; no automatic mutation replay.

diagrams.title: Authorize every action before executing any
diagrams.caption: Agreed execution flow for an authenticated client operation. The core expands the selected GraphQL operation and checks original schema coordinates, so aliases and fragments do not rename authority. Any denied mutation action prevents all actions from beginning. Revocation is checked again at each dispatch admission. Earlier authorized effects are not rolled back if a later action fails. Enrollment and the in-process console have separately defined admission cases in the spec.

diagrams.title: Grant issuance, approval and revocation
diagrams.caption: Agreed bearer-credential lifecycle and revocation ordering. Anonymous enrollment creates only a pending request. Existing managers or the in-process console approve requests or create manual grants. Approved grants survive restart without automatic expiry; pending-request expiry does not expire them. Secret possession permits own-request status before and after its decision; revoked grants fail authentication. Digest uniqueness prevents retries from creating multiple grants. Already admitted actions may finish. This diagram is not a model-checking result.

diagrams.title: Agreed Swift framework and the alternative
diagrams.caption: The human selected the shared resilient Swift framework. Swift types and protocols are part of its stable published contract, with library evolution and module stability enabled from release one. The C-compatible alternative is not selected. Compatible provider binaries dynamically link the host-supplied framework; newer required symbols need a newer host and are checked before loading.

diagrams.title: Native schema and resolver contributions
diagrams.caption: The shared Swift framework as the loader applies it. Verify signed manifests and required framework versions before loading, then resolve the named principal class and require ProviderFactory conformance. Validate schema and authority metadata before starting the Provider. Requests/results use owned Swift values and async protocol methods. Independently built old/new binaries are verified through the native plugin seam (docs/verification/binary-compatibility.md); native trust is distinct from client capabilities.
